ratings_why.fun: One shared Recipe card that grows a line with each apprentice is easy to follow and fun to watch, and Phials on any unit make every board a new puzzle; the once-a-turn scaling clause is a reading tax.
ratings_why.distinct: A spell-making tribe whose payoff can be another tribe's carry, with moths gathering beside a lamp unit, plays unlike today's six; the growing shared spell is a known idea from other games.

verdict_why: The cards read and the fantasy shows in play; what is left is one missing ruling sentence and screen work, not a better design.

points.text: Burnet's line is an effect, not a keyword, and the Recipe only says what keyword lines do. Add one sentence: an effect line gives the unit that text permanently, and repeats don't stack.
The rule that a unit scales only on its first Phial each turn is hidden state. A small lamp mark on each unit that has had its scaled Phial this turn would make it readable at a glance.
Mortar Grinder counts two things, Phials on one unit and spells cast. "+1/+1 for each Phial it took this turn" would read in one pass.
Old Carbonaria keeps the ledger but the peppered moth's colour change is missing from the tribe; she could swap one Recipe line each turn, changing with the times.

standouts.why: Each apprentice adds a line to the master's recipe: the seed's lore is the mechanic, and the card reads in one line.
Mother Shipton turns your own Recipe into an omen on the enemy's biggest unit; clear, flavourful and it makes the Recipe matter in fights.
Psyche, the moth as soul, pours the Recipe onto her neighbours when she dies; short text, strong image.

weakest.why: Treacle Painter is a generic spell-to-token converter whose worth hangs on an unsettled shop spell price; the treacle-painted oaks don't show in what it does.
Atropos is a shop discount; the honey thief who slips into hives by smell is only in the name.
Mortar Grinder's two counts and random tie-break take a second read.

flags.note: How an effect line is granted by a Phial, and whether it stacks, isn't written.
Copied keywords from other tribes (Belly, Snap, Pack, Mire) each need a ruling as a Recipe line, as the designer notes.
Golden Pavonia with the Warden and Drawn neighbours spreads many casts a turn; worth the owner's eye on a simulated board.
